name: Question 1
problem:
Select the correct options in the truth table below and use this to determine whether $(P∧Q)∨(P⇒Q)$ is a tautology.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∧Q\,$ | $\,P⇒Q\,$ | $\,(P∧Q)∨(P⇒Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-4}} |

According to the table, $(P∧Q)∨(P⇒Q)$ 
{{field-5}}
always true. Therefore, it 
{{field-6}} 
a tautology.
worked_solution:
An expression is a tautology if it is always true, regardless of the inputs.

By completing the final column in the truth table below, we obtain the following:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,P∧Q\,$ | $\,P⇒Q\,$ | $\,(P∧Q)∨(P⇒Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

According to the table, $(P∧Q)∨(P⇒Q)$ 
$\text{isn't}$
always true. Therefore, it 
$\text{isn't}$
a tautology.
